title: NY Fed's Williams, Nov 23 (prepared text read at the issuer): inflation 'simply too high', 'the risk to maximum employment is dialed down, but the risk to achieving price stability is dialed up', 'still work to do'; no December meeting or hike size in the text; closes the UNKNOWN on 010
body:
# Williams, 'The Economic Mixdown', Bronx, November 23 2026 (prepared text, newyorkfed.org, read by WALTER)

- 'We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2 percent goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis. There is still work to do to get that done.'
- 'So, the risk to maximum employment is dialed down, but the risk to achieving price stability is dialed up.'
- Since the last meeting, data 'show that the economy has remained strong and that inflation has continued to run too high'.
- Outlook: real GDP about 2-3/4 percent this year and near that next year; unemployment down to about 4 percent over the next year; inflation about 3-1/2 percent this year, just above 2 percent next year.
- AI is a big driver and its effects are 'highly uncertain': the pace of the buildout could slow, which 'could reverse much of the AI-driven inflation'.
- **Not in the text read:** the December 8 to 9 meeting, a hike size, or financial conditions after last week's fall. CNBC says he did not directly address December (helper read). Q&A not read.

Also 11/20: Governor Cook's speech confirms she dissented in October, 'I preferred to raise the target range another 1/4 percentage point' (federalreserve.gov, read by helper). Waller 11/20 'Opening Remarks' not read; regional bank sites not swept.

Market pricing of December is ORACLE's (WQ-671 A); none is quoted here.
